mainEntity.name: Is it better to convert existing space or build an exterior addition for an in-law suite?

acceptedAnswer.text: Building within an existing floor plan involves converting spaces like garages, basements, or unused formal areas, whereas an attached addition expands the home's exterior footprint with new foundation and framing. Interior conversions generally cost less and avoid reducing yard space, but you give up existing utility, such as indoor parking or storage. New additions preserve your existing layout and allow completely customized dimensions, but they require ground disruption, exterior stucco and roofing integration, and setback reviews. Choosing between them depends on lot space, garage usage, and household budget.
acceptedAnswer.description: Converting existing space costs less and preserves yard area, while an exterior addition maintains your current interior layout but requires new foundation and exterior construction.
